stem: Maria, who owns two retail stores, says: "Yeah, that does sound interesting. Send me something?" With Calendar open in a second window, which close gets the meeting booked before you hang up?

options.label: A
options.text: "I'll send a calendar invite by email later today."
options.rationale: Nothing is booked when you hang up. The Salesforce flag stays FALSE until the invite goes out later, if it ever does.

options.label: B
options.text: "Let me know which day works best for you."
options.rationale: An open-ended close leaves the work with the buyer and gives her no two times to choose between.

options.label: C
options.text: "Two 20-minute slots next week: Tuesday 10:00 or Wednesday 10:30. Which works to walk through it with your bookkeeper?"
options.rationale: Two specific times in one sentence, and the invite can go out while Maria is still on the line. This is how M.G. closed her on GC-01.

options.label: D
options.text: "I'll follow up next week with some options."
options.rationale: "I'll follow up" is the line that lost GC-10 and GC-11. Neither buyer replied again.

stem: A rep in your pod tells you: "I always pick the slots after the call ends — I want to double-check my own calendar first." What does that habit cost, judging by the Gong and Salesforce data?

options.label: A
options.text: The Salesforce flag stays FALSE that day, and buyers re-engage about as rarely as after "I'll follow up".
options.rationale: Picking the slots after the call is "I'll follow up" under another name. The flag stays FALSE that day, and buyers reply about as rarely.

options.label: B
options.text: Nothing. The buyer accepted, so the booking is the same.
options.rationale: The booking may still happen, but the Next_Step_Booked__c flag stays FALSE on the day of the call.

options.label: C
options.text: It is fine if the rep sends the invite within 24 hours.
options.rationale: On GC-11 the rep sent the invite the next morning, and the buyer never replied.

options.label: D
options.text: It is better. Checking the calendar twice prevents double-booking.
options.rationale: With Calendar open in a second window you already see your free times. A clash can be fixed with a new invite; a buyer who has gone cold usually can't.

stem: You have read out two times and the buyer says "Tuesday works." What do you do next while they are still on the call?

options.label: A
options.text: Thank them and end the call. Confirm by email tomorrow.
options.rationale: The buyer has said yes on the call. Send the invite now, while they are still there.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask whether they want a reminder 1 day before.
options.rationale: A reminder is a nice extra. The invite during the call comes first.

options.label: C
options.text: Pivot to a second pitch prop while you have their attention.
options.rationale: Pitching a second product now puts the booking at risk. Lock in the next step first and pitch on the booked call.

options.label: D
options.text: Click Send invite in Calendar, then log the next step in Salesforce and click Save so Next_Step_Booked__c turns TRUE.
options.rationale: Send the invite from Calendar and save the next step in Salesforce so that Next_Step_Booked__c turns TRUE. Then check with the buyer that the invite arrived.
